subject: History
description: Life of Buddha, Councils, sects, Ashoka's patronage

questions.stem: Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment — becoming the Buddha — under a peepal tree at:
questions.explanation: Four major sites of Buddhism — Lumbini (birth, Nepal), Bodh Gaya (enlightenment, Bihar), Sarnath (first sermon, UP), Kushinagar (mahaparinirvana, UP). The Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya is a descendant of the original one. The Mahabodhi Temple is a UNESCO WHS. Buddha's first sermon at Sarnath, the 'Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta', set the 'Wheel of Dharma' in motion.

questions.stem: The four Noble Truths of Buddhism begin with the truth that:

options.option_text: Craving is the cause of suffering
There is a way out of suffering
The way is the Eightfold Path

questions.explanation: The Four Noble Truths: 1) Dukkha — suffering exists. 2) Samudaya — craving (tanha) is its cause. 3) Nirodha — suffering can cease. 4) Magga — the path to cessation (the Noble Eightfold Path). The Eightfold Path — right view, intention, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness, concentration — is the practical core of Buddhist discipline.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Fourth Buddhist Council, under royal patronage, was held during the reign of:
questions.explanation: Kanishka I (~2nd century CE) patronised the Fourth Buddhist Council — typically placed at Kashmir (Kundalavana / Harwan) — the council that formalised the Mahayana school. Ashoka patronised the Third Council at Pataliputra (~250 BCE). The First Council was at Rajagriha soon after Buddha's death; the Second at Vaishali. Ajatashatru supported the First Council.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Ashoka's son and daughter who helped spread Buddhism to Sri Lanka were:
questions.explanation: Mahendra (Mahinda) — Ashoka's son — led the first Buddhist mission to Sri Lanka (~3rd century BCE), accompanied later by his sister Sanghamitra with a sapling of the original Bodhi tree. She also ordained the first Sri Lankan women into the Bhikkhuni Sangha. Sri Lanka has been a Theravada Buddhist stronghold since then.

questions.stem: Nalanda — the great Buddhist university destroyed in the 12th century by Bakhtiyar Khilji — flourished chiefly under:
questions.explanation: Nalanda Mahavihara — founded in the 5th century CE under the Guptas (Kumaragupta I), further expanded by Harshavardhana and the Palas. At its peak it had 10,000 students (including from China, Korea, Japan, Tibet, South-East Asia), a nine-storey library, and was India's leading centre of Buddhist learning. Destroyed in 1193 by Bakhtiyar Khilji. A modern Nalanda University was re-established in 2014.

questions.stem: The two main sects of Buddhism are Theravada (the older, 'Southern') and:
questions.explanation: Theravada (literally 'teaching of the elders') — older, closer to early Buddhism; dominant in Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand, Cambodia, Laos. Mahayana ('Great Vehicle') — later sect that emerged around the 1st century BCE; emphasises the Bodhisattva ideal; dominant in China, Japan, Korea, Vietnam. Vajrayana (a Mahayana branch) — dominant in Tibet and Mongolia. Digambara / Svetambara are the two sects of Jainism.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Sanchi Stupa — one of the oldest stone structures in India — is located in:
questions.explanation: Sanchi — near Vidisha, Madhya Pradesh — its Great Stupa was commissioned by Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE and later enlarged under the Shungas. The four elaborately-carved toranas (gateways) are Satavahana-era additions. UNESCO WHS 1989. Sanchi's lion-capital style of Ashokan pillars inspired India's national emblem (from Sarnath).
